key_insight: CompMat-Bench benchmarks AI agents on realistic computational materials science steps by precomputing simulation inputs and outputs, enabling practical evaluation without rerunning expensive experiments.
engineering_relevance: The benchmark helps researchers compare agent quality on materials workflows and identify whether failures stem from scientific reasoning or tool-use issues, which is useful for building reliable autonomous research systems.
method: Built 94 tasks from recent computational materials papers.
Reproduced simulation inputs and results in advance to create fixed-rule ground truth.
Evaluated single tasks and multi-step workflows under full vs reduced methodological guidance.
evidence_signal: With full guidance on single tasks, agents based on three LLMs achieved 66.0–90.4% pass rates across 94 tasks, with performance dropping under longer workflows and reduced guidance.
watch_item: Because the benchmark uses reproduced steps rather than live simulations, results may not fully capture end-to-end robustness in real experimental or computational pipelines.
paper_title: CompMat-Bench: Benchmarking AI Agents for Computational Materials Science
